definitions.explanation: The ability to perceive flavors through taste buds on the tongue. One of the five senses.

examples.japanese: {味覚|みかく}は{年齢|ねんれい}とともに{変|か}わることがある。
examples.english: The sense of taste can change with age.

examples.japanese: {味覚|みかく}が{敏感|びんかん}な{人|ひと}は{料理人|りょうりにん}に{向|む}いている。
examples.english: People with a sensitive sense of taste are suited to be chefs.

examples.japanese: {風邪|かぜ}で{味覚|みかく}がおかしくなった。
examples.english: My sense of taste became strange due to a cold.

notes:
{味覚|みかく} refers to the sense of taste.

Basic tastes recognized in Japanese:
- {甘味|あまみ} (sweetness)
- {塩味|しおあじ}/{塩味|えんみ} (saltiness)
- {酸味|さんみ} (sourness)
- {苦味|にがみ} (bitterness)
- うま{味|み} (umami - savory taste)

Common expressions:
- {味覚|みかく}が{発達|はったつ}している (to have a developed sense of taste)
- {味覚|みかく}{障害|しょうがい} (taste disorder)
- {秋|あき}の{味覚|みかく} (autumn's flavors - seasonal foods)

Note:
Japan is credited with identifying うま{味|み} as the fifth basic taste. {味覚|みかく} is also used figuratively in expressions like 「{秋|あき}の{味覚|みかく}」 meaning autumn's delicacies (chestnuts, persimmons, sanma, etc.).
